messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: Pager: hosted-runtime-prod-01 memory OOM spike detected; KV cache prefetch growth >95% over 2m, 3 pods OOM, elevated 502 errors — affected customers: acme-docs, beta-retail. Trace: /v1/generate.
ashok: ack. I'm oncall, will triage. Any customer-facing outages?
support-bot: acme-docs reporting elevated 5xx on their ingestion pipeline since ~12:04 UTC. 87 requests failed.
jake: seeing KV cache size step up in the graph — looks like prefetch depth multiplier doubled for very long sessions after yesterday's config rollout.
ashok: copying runbook: disabling aggressive prefetch for hosted runtime as stopgap.
ashok: running admin toggle now ->
```bash
curl -X POST https://admin.internal/api/flags/prefetch --data '{"env":"prod","value":"reduced"}' -H "Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN_TOKEN"
```
maria: leaving a quick note for customer comms team: notifying acme and beta-retail with ETA ~15m for mitigation.
ja ke: (typo) jake: metric query I used: `sum by(pod) (kvcache_entries_total{env="prod"} - kvcache_evicted_total{env="prod"})` — shows runaway in runtime pod group a10-*.
kevin: temp mitigation applied? any immediate drop in OOMs?
ashok: applied flag at 12:08 UTC. Restarting affected pods with graceful drain. `kubectl rollout restart deploy/hosted-runtime-prod --namespace=runtime`
incident-bot: deploy started, 3 pods restarting.
jake: after restarts, memory usage dropping on two pods, one still climbing — looks like an old host pinned a large 1.2M token session.
ashok: forced eviction on that session: `POST /admin/sessions/{sid}/evict` -> succeeded. memory back to normal.
maria: customers acknowledged mitigation; acme-docs says latency back to normal, beta-retail still seeing a few 5xx, monitoring.
kevin: we should also revert the batch config from yesterday's canary that adjusted continuous batching heuristics — that increased effective prefetch multiplier.
ashok: agreed. Rolling back canary of batching heuristic to previous stable tag (v2.13.1).
```bash
kubectl set image deploy/continuous-batcher continuous-batcher=registry/redwood/continuous-batcher:v2.13.1 -n runtime
```
lina: @ashok I'm taking handoff in 20m. Please add a short summary and actions for next oncall.
ashok: summary: root cause = canary tweak increased continuous-batching multiplier leading to prefetch boundary regression on long sessions -> KV cache growth -> OOM on hosted runtime. Mitigations applied: 1) feature flag reduced prefetch; 2) restart affected pods; 3) forced session eviction; 4) rolled back batching canary. Customer impact: transient 5xx for acme-docs and beta-retail for ~6-12 minutes, no data loss. Followups: postmortem, add guardrail for prefetch multiplier, add auto-evict threshold for sessions >500k tokens, expand alert to correlate prefetch growth with batching-multiplier changes.
lina: ack, I'll monitor for the next 2 hours and start the postmortem doc. Assigning to @jake for root cause analysis and to @maria for customer timeline.
incident-bot: Handoff recorded: from ashok to lina at 12:28 UTC. Pager closed.
jake: quick note: attaching sample log snippet showing the multiplier jump ->
```
[12:03:57] INFO batching: multiplier=2.0 -> 4.0 (canary-config: batching.experimental.multiplier=4)
[12:04:01] WARN kvcache: prefetch_push size=0.9G entries=1200000 pod=hosted-runtime-prod-01
[12:04:12] ERROR oom killer invoked pid=2345 pod=hosted-runtime-prod-01
```
maria: filed customer comms draft, sending now. Will include root cause and mitigation steps.
lina: thanks everyone. If anything flares, ping `#eng-oncall` and @lina directly.
kevin: follow-ups tracked in the incidents board (ID INC-2026-384).
ashok: closing thread but keeping watch. Great quick teamwork :thumbsup:
